title: Diagnosis: a clear support report and a verified correction
goal: Explain the 1441-minute refusal, prepare a safe reproduction and confirm valid writing still works.

prerequisites.text: 1c-enterprise.a 5; A1–A2: separate infobase, catalogs, references and documents; synthetic data only.

sections.title: Separate symptom from hypothesis
paragraphs: “R1 does not save after−1” is an observation;“the infobase is broken” is a hypothesis. Record expectation, safe reproduction steps, version and outcome. Reproduce on a synthetic copy. Do not attach real data publicly when the issue occurs only there; prepare a minimal sanitized example and agree on access separately.

Start with an observation: in my training copy, a request with valid references rejects 1441 minutes and accepts 45. This is more precise than claiming the database is broken. Record program, version, window, action and expected 0..1440 range. Use own synthetic identities; do not attach real databases or screenshots containing other people’s information.

sections.title: Observation, rule and control
paragraphs: Not every refusal is a program defect.

code.source:
Observed:1441 rejected
Rule:0..1440
Control:45 accepted and reread
After refusal:stored 45
code.output: A normal input refusal is explained and data preserved.

sections.title: Classification narrows diagnosis
paragraphs: Distinguish business-rule rejection, permission denial, configuration defect, environment unavailability and persistence failure. A generic “error” does not prescribe a fix. Compare valid and invalid inputs and inspect state. Do not change role, platform and data simultaneously: the cause of improvement becomes unknowable.

Permission refusal and input validation are different. The reader should not write even valid 31; the administrator should write 45 but be refused 1441. Compare role and input separately. Changing privileges, platform and data simultaneously destroys causal interpretation. Correct clear input errors rather than disabling object validation.

sections.title: Provide the minimum sufficient package
paragraphs: Include case ID, time, versions, expected/actual, safe message excerpt and control total. Exclude passwords, tokens, full databases and third-party configurations. Review screenshots before sharing. Restrict technical logs; publish only necessary classification and a synthetic example.

A useful report includes case ID, time, platform/configuration, own copy, role, safe steps, expectation, observation, state after refusal and completed controls. Exclude passwords, tokens, licenses, full databases and third-party configurations. Share only the relevant safe message, not arbitrary full-screen or raw-log contents.

sections.title: An unbounded hypothesis
paragraphs: Use specific inputs, roles, versions and repeatable controls.

code.source: It seemed to work after changing everything.

sections.title: Bound independent repairs
paragraphs: An operator may correct input under a clear rule, but must not run unknown processors or mass cleanup. Preserve work and contact the responsible role. After a fix, repeat the original case and a nearby positive control. Closing the ticket without retesting does not prove the issue disappeared or data survived.

Close the issue by repeating the original case and a valid control. After refusing 1441, this saved request remains 45. Valid changes should persist on rereading. Correcting learner input differs from fixing a program defect: the former needs no configuration change; the latter needs its own revised work/test while preserving the source.

sections.title: Check your explanation
paragraphs: Every write refusal is called database corruption. Compare actual input with the rule and run a valid control.
A report includes the entire database and secrets. Share minimal synthetic reproduction and a safe message.
An issue closes without rereading data. Repeat the original and valid cases, checking persistent state.

selfcheck.feedback: Exclude secrets and other people’s data.

selfcheck.prompt: Compare reader 31 denial with administrator 1441 refusal in two reports.
selfcheck.feedback: Permissions and validation separated without bypassing controls.

practice.title: From 1441 refusal to a reproducible report and recheck
practice.task: Compare reader 31 denial with administrator 1441 refusal in two reports.
practice.environment: Own original service desk; synthetic records only. No real Nexus accounts, Windows identities or external services are changed.
practice.externalRoute: Official installed 1C Enterprise/Designer of your own separate training copy

steps.title: Select an own saved request
steps.action: Open an own 45-minute request as the teaching administrator and record number/date/references/version. Retain older work.
steps.troubleshooting: If absent, create an own valid one without altering other records.
steps.before: Earlier A5 work/provenance and a verified separate-copy route are retained.

steps.title: Reproduce the input refusal
steps.action: Enter 1441 and attempt writing. Read the duration message, retain its safe text and return the open form to 45. Keep validation enabled.
steps.expected: Invalid input rejected with an understood reason.
steps.troubleshooting: If another failure occurs, record it rather than substituting the expected message.

steps.title: Verify persisted state
steps.where: Enterprise → close form → reopen own number
steps.action: Do not save 1441. Reopen and verify stored 45 plus references/other fields.
steps.why: Separate persisted state from unsaved input.
steps.troubleshooting: Never confirm saving invalid input; correct it or discard the unsaved edit.
steps.before: Invalid input rejected with an understood reason.

steps.title: Write a short report
steps.action: Record case ID, time/versions, role, own copy, input 1441, expected refusal, observed message, retained 45 and the valid control. Remove personal/license data and secrets.
steps.why: Make the experiment reproducible and safe to share.
steps.expected: A minimal report exists without transferring the base.
steps.troubleshooting: Do not attach full logs/databases or run an unknown repair processor.

steps.title: Close only the verified result
steps.action: Repeat valid 45, writing and rereading. State that normal input validation was confirmed without a program fix. Preserve original/new cases separately for an actual defect.
steps.expected: Positive control works; negative case preserves state.
steps.troubleshooting: Do not claim permissions/integration/server fixes outside the tested scope.
steps.before: A minimal report exists without transferring the base.

criteria: Specific input and rule boundary identified.
Safe report distinguishes refusal and preservation.
Permissions and validation separated without bypassing controls.
Actual versions and distinct own-copy paths; synthetic identities and before/after values.
Allowed/refused cases, completed controls and explicit untested scope; no secrets.
Use the second worked case to identify the unsafe or unproved condition. Never perform destructive restoration over existing work.
